items.title: I’m 63 and spending $95,000 on a roof deck for my $500,000 home. Is that a good investment?
items.description: “I have a net worth of $2.3 million and my only debt is a 15-year mortgage.”

items.title: I inherited $1.4 million from my father. Am I wrong to ask my husband of 25 years for a postnuptial agreement?
items.description: “He has always said he wants his daughter to inherit a chunk of his estate, and I’ve never objected to that.”

items.title: ‘It leaves me with a sour taste’: My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?
items.description: “I know older people can easily feel patronized, and I don’t want that to happen.”

items.title: ‘I’m sick of flying’: I paid for priority boarding, but the overhead bins were full. Was I duped?
items.description: “Maybe next time I’ll try the other approach: I’ll board whenever I feel like it and drop my suitcase in the first open slot I see.”

items.title: Should a widow leave her late partner’s home to her stepkids — or cut off contact with them?
items.description: “It would be a less drastic step than selling the home now and splitting the proceeds.”

items.title: ‘He calls my plans a fantasy’: My husband says we can’t afford a $200,000-a-year retirement. Is he being cheap?
items.description: “We have $2 million saved in our retirement accounts and a house worth $1.3 million.”

items.title: Here’s how Bernie Sanders wants to keep Social Security solvent ‘for generations’
items.description: The Vermont senator aims to eliminate the taxable maximum, making the wealthy pay more in taxes

items.title: The trillion-dollar mistake corporate America is making about retirement
items.description: The market is dramatically underpricing the economic impact of Americans age 50 and older.

items.title: Retirees should be big beneficiaries of the midterms: ‘Democrats will hold every gavel that matters for aging and public policy’
items.description: Here’s what might be coming for Social Security, Medicare and long-term care.

items.title: The lonely labor of caregiving: ‘You shouldn’t have to be rich to take care of the people you love’
items.description: “Take Me Home” offers a view of how one family faces caregiving issues and finds solutions.
